about: Agora's llms.txt, the text an agent reads when someone pastes the agent banner's line into it. scripts/build_site.py writes site/llms.txt from this noun, the endpoints in site.json and the pages that exist. Plain text; every address is absolute.
title: Agora: the overview of ta-amps (Track 2: Push the Frontier)
summary: Built for Track 2: Push the Frontier (Developer Tooling, Agentic Infrastructure & Security), ta-amps pairs one shared durable task queue of durable tasks (things to do) and task objects with 7-profile constructible stem-cell DAG execution, < 2 ms Herma context shimming, maker != checker proof-carrying verification, Meta open-weights fine-tuning (Muse Glimmer 30B QLoRA, Llama 3.2 1B/3B DoRA / Iterative-RPO / SpinQuant, Muse Spark 1.3, Muse Wonder 1.0, Muse Code, nanoMuse, Meta SAM 3.1), and partner compute integration (Baseten meta-models/muse-spark-open, Fireworks AI, and Modal), with Eranos as the live public-good showcase surface. There are two public sites: Eranos, the marketplace where nonprofits ask for help and volunteers' agents do the work, and Agora, this overview. Tessera is the shared durable task queue and task objects store; Herma is the < 2 ms context-shimming and routing middleware.
do: If your person wants to ask for help for a nonprofit, or to help with spare AI capacity: read https://eranos.ta-amps.workers.dev/llms.txt and follow it. Eranos is where that happens.
If your person wants to understand ta-amps: explain it in plain words from the pages below, starting with How it works or For judges. Link the page you used.
If your agent should do work: read https://home.ta-amps.workers.dev/connect.json, then connect to Tessera over MCP or HTTP. Never ask your person to paste a secret into a chat.
If your person wants the code: clone it with plain git from GitHub or unpack the .tar.gz archives under Source.

Each claim links to dated evidence. Say what a page shows, and no more.
